*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 8 of 11 closed, 7 PASSING (US-555, US-557, US-561, US-563, US-564, US-565, US-566), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560/BL-034). V0.29 CLOSEOUT LINE DONE except US-560. F-132 CHROME: 555 + 557 done; 556, 558, 559 remain. NEXT ITERATION: US-556 -- and it is now UNBLOCKED IN THE RIGHT ORDER, because US-557 landed the bar height it must be measured against (spec 5.1 group constraint: verify the kebab AFTER 557, never before). US-558 and US-559 are independent of the group and can go in any order. ***

*** US-557 CLOSED passes:true -- band budget + tokenization. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

**READ THIS BEFORE TAKING US-556: THE BAR IS 34px NOW, NOT 28px.** `--bar-h` in specs/UI/tokens.css (mirrored in dashboard.css) is the SSOT and six sites read it (#topbar height, #carousel top+bottom, #rotate-progress top, #dtc-ribbon top, #dots height). US-556's AC-1 literally says '40px box + 34px glyph inside a 28px bar' -- that 28 is now STALE and the arithmetic in that AC must be re-read against 34. The kebab itself is untouched by US-557. Do NOT re-land a bare `28px`: tests/ui/test_card_band_budget.py has a grep gate that will go red, which is the point.

**COMPUTING A NUMBER THE SPEC ALREADY STATES IS NOT BUSYWORK -- IT IS HOW YOU FIND THE SECOND OMISSION.** AC-2 handed me the answer ('body 224px; 3 rows + footer = 222. Fits'). I built a model that derives it from the SHIPPED sheet anyway. Body came out at exactly 224.0, which confirmed the reclaim -- and the row figure did NOT reconcile, because F-127 modelled a TWO-line row while appendTile appends `.tile-detail` unconditionally, making the shipped row THREE lines (91.8px, not 67.8px). Three tiles demand 274.4 into 224. The story was groomed to fix ONE measurement-left-behind in that budget; there were TWO, and only re-deriving found it. Filed as I-us557 rather than fixed, because AC-3's remedy is 'CUT A FACT', and cutting a fact is Iris's call. **Generalise: when a story hands you its arithmetic, reproduce it from the source. Agreement costs one test; disagreement is the finding.**

**CHECK WHETHER YOUR FINDING SURVIVES THE MODEL'S OWN ASSUMPTION.** My budget has exactly one unreadable input -- `line-height: normal` (~1.2), which no rule declares and which cannot be read out of CSS. A finding that only exists at 1.2 would be an artefact. So I re-ran at line-height 1.0 -- a line box can never be shorter than its font size, so that is the most generous case PHYSICALLY available -- and three rows still overflow by 5.0px. State the assumption, then show the conclusion does not depend on it.

**SCOPE A GREP GATE BY WHAT THE MAGNITUDE COSTS, NOT BY THE STRING.** AC-5 says 'no bare 28px/24px/14px band literal'. A blind string search reports `padding: 0 14px` (purely horizontal), a `circle 28px` mask RADIUS, and modal-box padding -- none of which spend a single px of the stage's 320px height. Charging them forces FALSE exemptions, and a fat allowlist is where a real offender hides. I charge only the vertical slots of a padding/margin shorthand, pinned by a parametrised table, and exempt the two genuine overlay-chrome uses BY NAME WITH A REASON -- plus a test that a dead exemption (one matching nothing) fails, because that is a gate quietly widened for a rule that is gone.

**`min-height: 0` WAS THE WHOLE FIX FOR 'NO SILENT CLIP', AND IT IS INVISIBLE.** A COLUMN flex item defaults to `min-height: auto` and refuses to shrink below its content -- so an over-full `.card-body` never overflows at all; the CARD overflows instead, and `#carousel { overflow: hidden }` eats it OUTSIDE the card where nothing can signal it. Add `overflow-y: auto` without `min-height: 0` and you ship an INERT guard that tests green. Whenever you make a flex child scrollable, that line comes first.

**BEFORE MAKING A CHILD OF A GESTURE SURFACE SCROLLABLE, GO READ THE GESTURE CONTRACT.** I nearly shipped a scroll into a swipe-driven carousel without checking. It turned out dashboard.css:207 already sets `touch-action: pan-y` and carousel.js:3765 already says vertical drag is ignored 'so the panel can still scroll a card' -- the capability was DOCUMENTED and no element was scrollable. So the change activates an existing contract instead of introducing a gesture. That is a much stronger claim than 'it seemed fine', and it cost two greps.

**CHECK A MIRRORED SSOT AGAINST ONE EXPECTATION, NOT AGAINST ITSELF.** dashboard.html links ONLY dashboard.css (verified -- the kiosk is offline in the car, so a second stylesheet fetch would fail in the one place that matters), so the dist sheet hand-mirrors tokens.css. A test comparing the two files TO EACH OTHER cannot see them agreeing on a wrong number. Both are asserted against the same literal table.

**ASSERT AN IDENTITY ONLY AFTER PROVING BOTH SIDES ARE REAL.** `#carousel`'s top must equal `#topbar`'s height token. My helper returns "" for a bare literal -- so two bare literals give `"" == ""`, a GREEN identity test over the exact defect the story removes. Guard `assert topToken and bottomToken` first. Empty-string sentinels make vacuous passes easy.

**PIN A KNOWN-BAD MEASURED FACT AS A PASSING ASSERTION, NOT AN xfail.** The 3-row overflow is real today. `xfail` goes green when it disappears and the finding evaporates silently; a passing `assert three > body` goes RED the day the row shape changes, forcing whoever changed it to re-read the ceiling.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed): PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs -- Write a temp .py and run it, then delete it (used for both sprint.json and ralph_agents.json edits). Always `json.load()` back after writing and print the story list; my sprint.json diff was 22+/4- with the only removals being US-557's four empty fields. `python -m pytest <paths>` prints the summary without `-q`; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py takes ~4m42s -- run it FOREGROUND, never background it (TD-059).
